name: Bohol
tagline: A thousand grass-covered Chocolate Hills, the world's smallest primate, a jungle river cruise and the white-sand diving beaches of Panglao.
highlight: The Chocolate Hills stretching to the horizon in the dry season, when the grass turns brown.
shortDescription: A central Philippine island with the Chocolate Hills, Philippine tarsiers, Loboc River cruises, Baclayon church and the beaches and reefs of Panglao Island.
metaDescription: A Bohol travel guide: Chocolate Hills, tarsiers, Loboc River cruise, Baclayon Church, Panglao beaches and diving, Balicasag Island, where to stay, how to get there and a three-day plan.
goodFor: Families, beach lovers, nature, day tours

image.alt: The rounded brown Chocolate Hills stretching across Bohol

intro: Bohol is a round island in the Visayas, an easy hop from Cebu, and one of the country's most complete destinations for a short trip. Its main sights can be seen in a single-day loop by car or van, and its southwest tip, Panglao, has some of the best beaches and diving in the central Philippines.

The signature sight is the Chocolate Hills, more than 1,200 dome-shaped hills of nearly uniform size, covered in grass that turns chocolate brown in the dry season. A viewing deck at Carmen gives the best panorama. Other stops include the Philippine tarsier, one of the world's smallest primates, at a sanctuary in Corella, a lunch cruise on the calm Loboc River through jungle, and Baclayon Church, one of the oldest stone churches in the country, built by the Jesuits in the 16th century.

The 2013 earthquake damaged many churches, but restoration is well advanced. After a day of sightseeing, most visitors relax on Alona Beach or take a boat to Balicasag and Virgin Islands for snorkelling and a sandbar. Three days is a good stay.

attractions.text: More than 1,200 conical hills between 30 and 120 metres tall, best seen from the viewing complex in Carmen.

attractions.name: Philippine tarsier

attractions.text: A tiny nocturnal primate with enormous eyes, seen at a sanctuary where visitors must be silent and cannot use flash.

attractions.name: Loboc River
attractions.text: A calm river lined with palms, with lunch cruises on floating restaurants.

attractions.name: Baclayon Church
attractions.text: A coral-stone Jesuit church from 1595, one of the oldest in the country.

attractions.name: Alona Beach
attractions.text: The main beach on Panglao, with restaurants, dive shops and white sand.

attractions.name: Balicasag Island
attractions.text: A marine sanctuary with coral walls.
